unite_adi: REGULAR UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 10-LEVEL: B1.2 THEME 5: LIFE IN THE NEIGHBOURHOOD, CITY & SOCIAL LIFE

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students conduct an interview with a person from their neighbourhood such as a driver, a chemist, a neighbour, an officer etc. about past experiences of these people in the city in terms of public transportation, the pros and cons of different types of transportation in the neighbourhood and city, getting help from services in the neighbourhood and the city and social life. Students begin by preparing interview questions. Next, they elicit and decide the questions. Then, they choose the person for the interview. They may use avatars or AI to create characters for the interviews. The interview should include creative elements, such as charts, or videos, and students will present their findings in class. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''life in the neighbourhood, city & social life with its components such as activities to do in attractions and recreational places (cafes, cinemas; gyms, sports clubs); getting help from services (pharmacies, hospitals etc); pros and cons of different types of transportation in the neighbourhood and city'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student of an upper secondary school in year 10 may know what life in the neighbourhood & city & social life, activities, events, places and transportation in the neighbourhood & city & social life mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students of an upper secondary school in year 10, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''life in the neighbourhood, city & social life'' in English from previous themes and/or years such as ''a house, hospital, cafe, bus, a shop, to go to cinema and so on'' and also some structures such as ''Where do you live? I live in a flat. What did you do at home yesterday?'' in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''life in the neighbourhood, city & social life with its components such as activities to do in attractions and recreational places (cafes, cinemas; gyms, sports clubs); getting help from services (pharmacies, hospitals, etc.); pros and cons of different types of transportation in the neighbourhood and city'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss about the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To talk about activities, services, and transportation options in the city and neighbourhood by listing pros and cons in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: City Life Discussions The teacher divides the class into three groups with specific topics: Group 1: Activities in attractions and recreational places (e.g., cafés, cinemas, gyms). Group 2: Getting help from services in the neighbourhood and city (e.g., pharmacies, hospitals). Group 3: Pros and cons of different types of transportation in the neighbourhood and city. Each group creates a list of pros and cons using the target vocabulary (e.g., ''Public transport saves time but is often crowded'', or ''Chatting with friends at a café feels relaxing but can be expensive''). Groups present their ideas to the class, and other students ask questions such as, ''Why do you think it is reliable?'' or ''Isn’t it time-consuming?'' After the discussion, each student writes a short paragraph and explains if s/he agrees or disagrees with one idea and why. The teacher provides feedback on accuracy, use of target vocabulary, and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To describe past activities in different places in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: What Were We Doing? The teacher writes some target words on the board for different places: At the café: drinking tea, chatting with friends. At the gym: lifting weights, doing pilates. At the cinema: watching a movie, eating popcorn. The teacher gives an example and writes it on the board: ''I was drinking tea at the cafe''. Then, students come to the board one by one and write their own sentences (e.g., ''We were watching a movie at the cinema''.). Next, the teacher writes a question and answer on the board: ''What were you doing at the cafe?'' ''I was chatting with friends''. Students practise asking and answering questions in a chain drill game format: one student asks the next, and so on. The teacher gives constructive and supportive feedback on accuracy and pronunciation. Students 340 THE ENGLISH LANGUAGE CURRICULUM reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
